GitHub Copilot CLI just changed how a solo builder ships.

What changed: Copilot CLI's new /fleet mode takes one objective and splits it into parallel work for a team of agents — not one bigger chat.

What it does: it decomposes your prompt into dependent and independent tasks, runs the independent ones at the same time, then synthesizes the results.

Why it matters: tester, docs, and code move together instead of waiting in line behind one thread.

Try this: this week, give /fleet one real objective — a refactor, a doc pass, a test sweep — and watch it split the work.

text:
GPT-5.6, Claude Opus 5, Sonnet 5 — pick your model like a tool, not a hype cycle.

Every lab shipped this month. The story isn't the benchmark chart. It's that speed, cost, and fit now matter as much as raw power.

Fast and cheap (Luna, Sonnet) wins for quick drafts and small fixes. Heavy reasoning (Sol, Opus) wins for long tasks and real judgment calls.

The move: match the model to the job, not the headline.

Save this the next time you open a new chat and default to the biggest name out of habit.
